chunks: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj narrated from Abān ibn Taghlib, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “What do you say about a man who cuts off one finger of a woman? How much is due for it?” He said: “Ten camels.” I said: “If he cuts off two?” He said: “Twenty.” I said: “If he cuts off three?” He said: “Thirty.” I said: “If he cuts off four?” He said: “Twenty.”

I said: “Glory be to Allah! He cuts off three, so thirty are due from him; then he cuts off four, so twenty are due from him? This used to reach us while we were in Iraq, and we would dissociate ourselves from whoever said it, and we would say: the one who said it was a shayṭān.”

So he said: “Take it gently, O Abān. This is how the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله ruled. Indeed, a woman is equal to a man in compensation up to one-third of the diyah; then when it reaches one-third, the woman returns to one-half. O Abān, you confronted me with qiyās, and the sunnah (prophetic tradition), when subjected to analogy, destroys the religion.”

key_terms.إِلَى النِّصْفِ: returning to half, referring to the woman’s compensation after the threshold
key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: blood money or financial compensation for bodily injury or killing
key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: the normative prophetic ruling and transmitted practice
key_terms.الْقِيَاسِ: analogical reasoning used to extend rulings by comparison
key_terms.ثُلُثِ الدِّيَةِ: one-third of the blood-money threshold at which the ruling changes
key_terms.مِنَ الْإِبِلِ: camels, the compensation unit mentioned in the ruling

ai.seo_question: Why does compensation for a woman’s fingers change after reaching one-third of the diyah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on compensation for a woman’s injured fingers and explains that her diyah matches a man’s up to one-third, after which it returns to half. It also strongly rejects qiyās in deriving rulings against the established sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.
